text:
jess: Quick sync — proposing a unified eviction lifecycle API to replace ad-hoc signals in prefix cache + KV. Current pain: duplicate backoff code, inconsistent token usage, and a few weird rehydrate-stale incidents.

ravi: I like the idea. Can you sketch the event set?

matt: Proposed events: ADMIT, SOFT_EVICT, HARD_EVICT, TOUCH, REVALIDATE, and REJECT_STALE. Each event carries (epoch, seq, token, origin). Minimal but explicit.

olivia: Need precise ordering semantics. If SOFT_EVICT followed by ADMIT with higher seq but same epoch — is that allowed?
jess: Yes. Semantics: seq monotonic within an epoch. ADMIT increments seq to indicate fresh residency intent. HARD_EVICT increments epoch (invalidate older seqs/tokens). If a handler sees event with (epoch < local_epoch) or (epoch == local_epoch && seq <= local_seq) treat as no-op.
sam: How do tokens work with tombstones? We had a past bug where a tombstone write wasn't correlated with lease state and a lagging node rehydrated stale keys.
matt: Token is a compact eviction nonce (u64). When we emit SOFT_EVICT/HARD_EVICT we persist token with the lease. Any compaction/tombstone op includes that token. During rehydrate, nodes compare tokens and if mismatch return REJECT_STALE and trigger authoritative sync.
kai: Storage cost? Persisting a 8-byte token per-lease seems fine. But how do we keep token atomic with the tombstone write?
jess: Persist lease record (epoch, token, seq) in the metadata store in same transaction/order as eviction intent. Tombstone writes reference token. We also append an eviction-intent record to a CAS-backed ledger for audit and recovery.
ravi: What about performance? Adding token checks in the hot read path could be costly, especially when many requests avoid lease lookup due to prefix pins.
matt: Important: token compare happens only when a lease check is performed (rehydrate or lease refresh), not per-token. For hot cache hits we still avoid the metadata fetch. We'll add a microbench and a tail-run on canary cluster.
olivia: Rollout strategy? We can't break Dedicated customers mid-flight.
jess: Staged rollout: 1) emit lifecycle events read-only (telemetry) 2) enable observers that flag mismatches and optionally auto-reject based on heuristics 3) gated opt-in enforcement per deployment 4) global enforcement + cleanup. Provide per-deployment toggle for Dedicated.
sam: Tests: need heavy-chaos property tests — reorder events, drop HARD_EVICT, rehydrate from lagging node, assert REJECT_STALE until authoritative sync runs. Also add e2e where tombstone compaction and rehydrate race.
matt: I'll put together a harness that fuzzes (epoch, seq, token) transitions and simulates network partitions. Expect to see ~5 failure modes we currently have.
kai: UX: ops need visibility. Can we surface a per-prefix timeline in Console and an endpoint to force reconcile?
ravi: Yes please. A timeline with last N events + trace IDs would make debugging much faster.
jess: We'll emit lifecycle events with trace IDs to telemetry. Console shows timeline + a reconcile button that triggers authoritative rehydrate and token reconciliation.
olivia: What about allocator hints and fairness? Our demote/fairness code sometimes triggers cross-tenant spillovers. Lifecycle events should carry a hint field for allocator priority.
matt: Add optional hint_priority enum on SOFT_EVICT; allocator uses it for scoring. No correctness change.
sam: Edge cases: multi-node concurrent ADMITs and near-simultaneous HARD_EVICT. How do we avoid split-brain where two nodes think they own prefix?
jess: Lease persistence model: authoritative lease in metadata store with epoch+holder. ADMIT requires writing lease holder with CAS; if CAS fails, ADMIT loses. HARD_EVICT bumps epoch so stale holders see mismatch and must yield.
ravi: Crash recovery: if node crashes after writing tombstone but before updating lease, we might be inconsistent.
kai: Ensure tombstone write first records token in lease store, then compaction references it. Use two-phase commit-like ordering but avoid long locks. We'll document the required atomic ordering and add reconciler that scans intents.
matt: Ops knobs: add a 'soft window' after SOFT_EVICT where reads fall back to shadow-read instead of immediate reject. Parameterizable per-deployment. Useful to reduce tail when transient GC runs.
jess: Canaries: single-shard opt-in with telemetry alerts for REJECT_STALE spikes and p99 regressions. We'll keep opt-in for Dedicated customers.
olivia: Action items: matt -> lifecycle proto + bench (EOW). ravi -> migration doc + customer opt-in plan (tomorrow). sam -> test harness seeds (3 core races). kai -> reconcile API spec + ledger schema. jess -> add RFC summary to rfc repo and schedule canary.
deploy-bot: Reminder: bench cluster reserved Thu 01:00 UTC.
jess: Thanks — if no objections I'll open a PR for read-only event emission today.
ravi: No objections. :thumbsup:
matt: On it.
sam: Thanks everyone.
